Introduction:

Too, too much, too many, and enough:

Too is a word used when something is more than you expected. (e.g., Last weekend, I went to the palace to see how modern and beautiful it is. Then, a few seconds later, I realized this place is much more luxurious than I had thought.)

Too much is a term that always refers to something uncountable. (e.g., There are too many people in this place; it's such a shame.)

Too many is the opposite of too much and refers to something countable. (e.g., My friend has too many different kinds of computers and laptops.)



So/such:

So is a word used to describe someone when they are very happy or when something is better than you expected.

Such can be used to describe both negative and positive situations. (e.g., It's such a beautiful day.)



Too and enough:

We use 'too' to say that something is more than we like or want. (e.g., These shoes are too big for me; I told you to lower the size already.)

SENTENCES WITH TOO, TOO MUCH, TOO MANY, AND ENOUGH

SPEAKING:



Today, I’m going to tell you about London in the UK. London has been known for a long time for its advanced technology and fresh environment. In terms of transportation, people can also save time. You know, in the UK, people don’t need to buy paper tickets; they can easily book tickets online for various forms of transport like buses or trains. In London, students can enjoy a good study environment and better transportation options. Finally, yes, of course I definitely agree to live there because studying there can bring me better experiences and skills, and I can also use public transport easily.

Replace it

In the end, she didn't like the decor and considered knocking down the wall.

A week later, the walls came down.

Rob:

There's space in the cellar and garage.

He had a great idea.

What if he knocked down the walls between the two areas to create more space for his kids?

He asked a friend to come over and help with the job, and the friend said, 'Sure.'

He had friends who had done similar work in the past.

Later, he successfully knocked down the walls.

His wife was disappointed and said she felt Rob had made a promise. Every time, he couldn't finish the final touches because he was too busy with household chores, his kids' football matches, and other stuff (both on weekends and weekdays).

He didn't want to hire a professional engineer because it was too expensive.

Finally, he says that you need to trust the process in your progress, and it will improve day by day.

Atonia: A, D
